record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Let us fix a certain algebraic type of a linear operator, i.e., its Segre characteristic (see above). Does there exist a Nijenhuis operator L in Rn with the following two properties: 1. L has compact support; 2. in a certain domain U ⊂ Rn, the algebraic type of L does not change and coincides with the given one? More generally, find necessary and sufficient conditions, in t erms of the Segre characteristic, for the existence of a Nijenhuis operator in Rn with the above properties. Notice that for semisimple operators L with real eigenvalues, the answer to the above question is positive. However, if some of the eigenvalues of L are complex, then L cannot have compact support. Also, one can easily construct an example of a Nijenhuis operator L with compact support which has the form of a Jordan block, e.g., L = ( y x 0 y ), on a certain disc. However, even for single Jordan blocks of size ≥ 3 the answer is unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A (1,1)-tensor field on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a smooth field $L$ of linear operators $L(x):T_x\mathbb{R}^n\to T_x\mathbb{R}^n$. Its Nijenhuis torsion is the (1,2)-tensor
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY],$$
where $X,Y$ are smooth vector fields and $[\,,\,]$ denotes the Lie bracket. The tensor $L$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if $\mathcal{N}_L \equiv 0$.

(b) The Segre characteristic of a linear operator $A$ on a complex vector space is the unordered tuple of sizes of its Jordan blocks, with blocks corresponding to the same eigenvalue grouped together; it encodes the conjugacy class of $A$ up to the values of the eigenvalues. We say a (1,1)-tensor $L$ on a domain $U\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ has constant algebraic type with Segre characteristic $\sigma$ if at every $x\in U$ the operator $L(x)$ (viewed over $\mathbb{C}$) has Segre characteristic $\sigma$.

(c) The support of $L$ is the closure of $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : L(x)\ne 0\}$. We say $L$ has compact support if this set is compact.

Problem. Fix an integer $n\ge 1$ and a Segre characteristic $\sigma$ of an $n\times n$ operator.

(1) Does there exist a Nijenhuis operator $L$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that:
    (i) $L$ has compact support, and
    (ii) there exists an open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ on which $L$ has constant algebraic type equal to $\sigma$?

(2) More generally, give necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed purely in terms of $\sigma$, for such a Nijenhuis operator to exist.

Known partial information: if $\sigma$ corresponds to a semisimple operator with only real eigenvalues, the answer to (1) is positive; if $\sigma$ involves any non-real (complex) eigenvalue, no such compactly supported Nijenhuis operator can exist. For a single $2\times 2$ Jordan block (e.g. $L=\begin{pmatrix} y & x\\ 0 & y\end{pmatrix}$ on a disc) the answer is positive. The case of a single Jordan block of size $\ge 3$ is what is principally in question.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on Nijenhuis geometry (e.g. work on gl-regular Nijenhuis operators and Nijenhuis operators with a unity, 2020–2024) develops local normal forms and studies algebraically generic points, but does not announce a solution to the global existence question of compactly supported Nijenhuis operators with prescribed Segre type, in particular for single Jordan blocks of size ≥ 3. No source found resolving the problem; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Develops local normal forms for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators around algebraically generic points without addressing compact-support global existence.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on local normal forms; global compact-support existence for non-trivial Jordan types is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis operators with a unity and F-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces study to cases of one real or two complex conjugate eigenvalues; no claim of resolving compact-support problem.
status_evidence.claim: No claim of solution to the compact-support problem for Jordan-block Segre types of size ≥ 3.
